etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English likely, likly, lykly, likliche, from Old English ġelīclīċ (“likely”) and Old Norse líkligr (“likely”), both from Proto-Germanic *līkalīkaz, equivalent to like +‎ -ly (adjectival suffix).

definitions.definition: Probable; having a greater-than-even chance of occurring.

quote.citation: 2009 May 24, Laura Miller, “Faking It”, in New York Times‎[1]:
quote.text: His parents — a restless, titanically self-involved father and a mother who cultivated her inner life in strict solitude — seem a much likelier source for his condition.

quote.citation: 2011 January 29, Ian Hughes, “Southampton 1 - 2 Man Utd”, in BBC‎[2]:
quote.text: Still, Saints looked the likeliest to make the breakthrough, and it came when Jonny Evans could only half-clear a long ball and Chaplow took full advantage.

definitions.definition: (as predicate, followed by to and infinitive) Reasonably to be expected; apparently destined, probable.

quote.citation: 2013 April 9, Andrei Lankov, “Stay Cool. Call North Korea’s Bluff.”, in New York Times‎[3]:
quote.text: People who talk about an imminent possibility of war seldom pose this question: What would North Korea’s leadership get from unleashing a war that they are likely to lose in weeks, if not days?

quote.citation: 2011 November 3, Chris Bevan, “Rubin Kazan 1 - 0 Tottenham”, in BBC Sport‎[4]:
quote.text: In truth, Tottenham never really looked like taking all three points and this defeat means they face a battle to reach the knockout stages - with their next home game against PAOK Salonika on 30 November likely to prove decisive.

definitions.definition: Appropriate, suitable; believable; promising, having a good potential.
Plausible; within the realm of credibility.

quote.citation: 2011 December 19, Kerry Brown, “Kim Jong-il obituary”, in The Guardian‎[5]:
quote.text: The DPRK propagated an extraordinary tale of his birth occurring on Mount Baekdu, one of Korea's most revered sites, being accompanied by shooting stars in the sky. It is more likely that he was born in a small village in the USSR, while his father was serving as a Soviet-backed general during the second world war.

definitions.definition: Leading with high probability to some specified outcome.

quote.citation: 1596, Edmund Spenser, An Hymne in Honour of Beautie:
quote.text: For love is a celestiall harmonie Of likely harts composed of starres concent

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English likely, likly, lykly, likliche, from Old English ġelīclīċe (“equally”) and Old Norse líkliga, glíkliga (“likely”), both from Proto-Germanic *līkalīka, equivalent to like +‎ -ly (adverbial suffix).

quote.citation: 2018 February, Robert Draper, “They are Watching You—and Everything Else on the Planet: Technology and Our Increasing Demand for Security have Put Us All under Surveillance. Is Privacy Becoming just a Memory?”, in National Geographic‎[6], Washington, D.C.: National Geographic Society, →ISSN, →OCLC, archived from the original on 14 June 2018:
quote.text: Dismounting on the sidewalk, their helmets still on, they fall into a lengthy conversation. Their dialogue is known only to them. But there is something the men themselves likely don’t know: About a mile away, from a windowless room, two other men are watching them.
